message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with information about the **Navy P-3 Orion**, which is a maritime patrol aircraft rather than a vessel (ship). Here's what I found:

## Overview

The **P-3 Orion** is a four-engine turboprop anti-submarine and maritime surveillance aircraft developed by Lockheed Martin. It has been a cornerstone of U.S. Navy maritime patrol operations for decades.

## Key Specifications

| Feature | Specification |
|---------|-------------|
| **Engines** | 4 × Allison T56-A-14 turboprops |
| **Shaft horsepower per engine** | 4,600 SHP |
| **Propeller type** | Hamilton Standard four-blade, full feathering & reversible |
| **Propeller diameter** | 13.5 feet |
| **Maximum speed** | 466 mph (dash speed) |
| **Endurance** | Up to 16-hour missions |
| **Crew capacity** | 12-person flight crew |
| **Total built** | 648 by Lockheed + 107 by Kawasaki (Japan) |

## Current Status (U.S. Navy)

The U.S. Navy has been phasing out its active-duty P-3C Orion fleet, replacing them with the **P-8A Poseidon**. As of recent reports:

- The last active-duty P-3C squadron (VP-40 "Fighting Marlins") completed its final deployments in 2019
- As of October 2025, only **6 active U.S. Navy P-3 Orions** remain in service with test and special mission units:
  - **VX-30**: 4 aircraft (150521, 160293, 162999, 163291)
  - **VXS-1**: 2 aircraft (158570, 158912)

## Distinctive Features

- **MAD "Stinger"**: A magnetic anomaly detector tail boom for detecting submarines
- **Bomb bay**: Internal weapons bay for torpedoes and depth charges
- **10 wing hard-points**: For missiles, mines, and other ordnance
- ** shortened fuselage**: 7 feet shorter than the commercial L-188 Electra it was based on

## International Operations

The P-3 Orion continues to serve with numerous international operators including:
- **Canada** (CP-140 Aurora/CP-140M)
- **Japan** (P-3C, being replaced by P-1)
- **Germany** (recently retired in 2025, transitioning to P-8A)
- **Portugal** (P-3C CUP+)
- **Argentina** (recently acquiring P-3Cs from Norway)
- **Greece** (modernizing P-3B fleet)
- **NOAA** (WP-3D for hurricane hunting)

## NASA Use

NASA operates a P-3B Orion as an airborne laboratory for scientific research, with a maximum research altitude of approximately 28,000 ft (capable of 32,000 ft under certain conditions).

Sources:
1. https://airbornescience.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/P-3B%20Experimenter%20Handbook%20548-HDBK-0001.pdf
2. https://www.p3orion.nl/news.html
3. https://www.twz.com/27565/the-navys-last-active-duty-p-3c-patrol-squadron-is-on-its-final-deployment
4. https://airandspace.si.edu/air-and-space-quarterly/issue-13/orion-p3
5. https://www.naval-technology.com/news/argentina-enriches-naval-surveillance-with-acquisition-of-p-3-orion/
